comment: A Spark's host checks: note, finding, explanation, commands and undo, all owned by the Controller. The vonkctl layout test checks the commands and undo lines appear in this order.
note: Run these on Alpha itself, in a terminal or over SSH, as a user with sudo; the Controller never changes a Spark. A check clears on the Spark's next report (about 2-3 minutes) once its change has taken effect: boot splash after a reboot; memory fragmentation is a reading and stays. Reasons and undo steps: https://github.com/CarstVaartjes/vonk-forge/blob/main/docs/operations/spark-host-checks.md

advice.finding: Active: snapd.service, snapd.socket, snapd.seeded.service; 26 MiB in use now.
advice.explanation: snapd keeps the snap store running and refreshing. The installed snaps are desktop apps and their runtimes only: bare, core22, core24, firefox, firmware-updater, gnome-42-2204, gtk-common-themes, mesa-2404 and 4 more.
commands: sudo systemctl disable --now snapd.service snapd.socket snapd.seeded.service
undo: sudo systemctl enable --now snapd.service snapd.socket snapd.seeded.service

advice.explanation: After memory fragments, the kernel raises its free-memory watermarks by this factor and reclaims ahead of need; that memory is missing from MemAvailable while the boost lasts. 0 turns the boost off, now and at every boot.

lines: vm.watermark_boost_factor is 15000. After memory fragments, the kernel raises its free-memory watermarks by this factor and reclaims ahead of need; that memory is missing from MemAvailable while the boost lasts. 0 turns the boost off, now and at every boot.

advice.explanation: The kernel compacts memory in the background. On a Spark a workload holds most of the unified memory, so this stalls the serving path and multi-Spark collectives. 0 stops only the background compaction, now and at every boot; compaction on demand and when loading starts still works.

advice.finding: The kernel command line has splash.
advice.explanation: Cosmetic: the boot splash hides kernel messages on the console of a headless Spark. Low impact; the change applies at the next boot.
commands: grep -lZE '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX(_DEFAULT)?=.*[ "]splash([ "]|$)' /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.d/*.cfg 2>/dev/null | sudo xargs -0 -r sed -i -E '/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX(_DEFAULT)?=/{:a;s/([ "])splash([ "]|$)/\1\2/;ta}' && sudo update-grub

advice.finding: 78.7 GiB of 116.7 GiB free is in blocks of 2 MiB or more (67%).
advice.explanation: The GPU driver takes unified memory in physically contiguous blocks of 2 MiB or more, so a load can run short while smaller free blocks remain. Compaction regroups free memory: the helper compacts once whenever loading starts on this Spark; to compact now, run this while no workload is loading.
commands: sync; echo 1 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches; echo 1 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory
